article.title: Omisión de marcadores de sujeto y objeto en conversación coreana
article.part: Contraste y dominio C2 — 대조와 C2 고급 운용
article.chapter: Norma, estilo y elección avanzada C2 — 규범·문체·C2 고급 선택

claims.summary: Kim (2009) empirically investigates the use and non-use of Korean subject marker ka and object marker lul in conversational Korean and proposes processing load and informational prominence as discourse-pragmatic factors.

The article abstract reports that ka/lul tend to occur overtly when subject/object represents processing load or informational prominence, and tend not to occur overtly when neither factor is represented.

The editorial advice is limited to the two markers and conversational analysis reported by Kim; it does not generalize to all Korean particles, written genres, or the examples removed from the previous article.
